entities.span: A direct email to Adzuna confirming the multi user reading of their terms is still open (residual from spec 0001's own follow-up list, line 199), and it bears directly on every number in this spec.

Feature 28 (spend visibility and gating polish) is the natural owner of a `select` policy on `usage_gate_counter` scoped to a user's own `account` rows, so a person can see their own remaining budget; not built here
rejected_spans: since nothing in this feature's own done when clause needs it

entities.span: **Also the natural owner of a retention rule** (fresh model review, 2026-09-03): rows accumulate one per account per week plus two per day plus two per month, indefinitely, with no pruning and the only removal path an unbuilt feature 31's account deletion cascade. This is now a privacy question, not just a storage one, since `usage_gate_counter` is listed under "Your job search usage" in the privacy notice (`src/features/legal/stored-fields.ts`) with no stated retention period for what it keeps forever.

`docs/observability/README.md`'s Status section should be rewritten once AC-11's threshold-breach creation delivery is proven (a resolved-issue delivery on 2026-09-03 proved the notification path, not the creation side): it was updated 2026-09-03 to record the four configured monitors and the connected alerts, but the smoke test is still pending and the section says so.
**Ticked 2026-09-03:** the creation delivery landed the same day and the Status section was rewritten with it.
Consider an absolute count threshold on the same two spans instead of the bare Threshold value
rejected_spans: because Sentry's Threshold form has no minimum sample count and a lone failure in a quiet 24 hour window reads as 100%; a count threshold would give a natural attempt floor at this app's volume (see AC-10, verified 2026-09-03)

**Already stale by the time this line is read**: spec 0001's item was ticked 2026-09-03, before this feature's own review rounds finished, and `docs/scope/scope.md`'s done when clause for feature 10 already names the non production qualifier; both checked directly rather than assumed on `/scope`'s reconciliation, 2026-09-04.

Adzuna publishes 2,500 a month under a heading reading "Default API access limits" on their terms of service page (`https://developer.adzuna.com/docs/terms_of_service`, checked 2026-09-04), not as a hard ceiling; the page states higher limits are offered "upon request for commercial applications with mutual benefit" ("We are very happy to increase limits for applications where we see mutual commercial benefit"), which a non-commercial project may not qualify for. Whether this project qualifies or whether Adzuna would consider an exception remains an open question if user count grows past what 2,000 a month comfortably serves.

**This feature's own migration was edited in place twice after CI had already pushed its original version to the hosted development project** (a third fresh model review, 2026-09-04): `20260902120000_usage_gating.sql` reached that project on 2026-09-03, then changed under both round-1 Majors' fixes and this round's collapsed lookup, and every push since silently skipped the file. Fixed here with `supabase db reset --linked` (see `verify.md:16`), because spec 0002 records this one project as holding synthetic data only. The general shape, an already-pushed migration edited in place leaving every hosted project it reached silently stale with no red check to catch it, outlives this feature and is recorded as spec 0002's follow-up instead, since that spec owns the migration workflow and invariant 5.
rejected_spans: because `supabase db push` applies by migration version, never content

entities.span: A real engaged kill switch reaching `checkUsageGate()` end to end could not be a committed integration test at first, and the reason was structural rather than a one off flake to route around. `app_settings` is a single row by design (spec 0002), so no test can hold its own copy of it, and `checkUsageGate()` reads that same row on every call, from every integration file. Vitest schedules different integration files to run in parallel by default, so ANY committed test that flips the switch races every other file's concurrent gate calls, not just one specific assertion.

Implemented the same day: a third Vitest project, `integration-serial` (`test/integration-serial/`, `sequence.groupOrder: 1`), added to `vitest.config.mts` and to `test:integration` in `package.json`. `groupOrder` orders PROJECTS, not the files inside one, so Vitest still schedules multiple files within `integration-serial` in parallel with each other. Merged into one file, `test/integration-serial/shared-global-state.test.ts`. Every future scenario needing this same real shared state belongs in that one file too, not a new one of its own. `groupOrder` still isolates the project from `integration`; `fileParallelism` now serialises the files within it. The scenarios still belong in one file, but because that stays simpler than splitting it, not because a split would be unsafe.
rejected_spans: Tried twice on 2026-09-03, once alongside `checkUsageGate()`'s own suite and once inside `kill-switch.test.ts` beside its own read of the row

since tests within one file are the only ordering actually guaranteed (confirmed against the installed `@vitest/runner` 4.1.11's own task runner), proved race free across five consecutive full `pnpm test:integration` runs after the merge
